onboarding.quote: no enterprise SSO is a real gap for a CRO of our size, and I'd want that before rolling it out to nine people.
onboarding.change: Add a SAML 2.0 / OIDC 'Sign in with your organization' option on the Sign-in card, and until it ships put a dated 'SSO — coming Qx' line under the sign-in form so IT sees a commitment.

onboarding.quote: I want to know whether... the demo shows the reset code on-screen tells me this isn't production-hardened for us yet.
onboarding.change: In the Forgot-password screen, hide the demo one-time code behind an explicit 'Reveal demo code' click instead of printing it inline, so it can never be screenshotted into a real workflow.

onboarding.quote: 'one workspace per client company' reads like the product isn't built for me, and I'd hesitate before signing up.
onboarding.change: Add a first-run toggle on the Create-workspace card: 'Filing for your own company' vs 'Filing on behalf of clients', and swap the 'Northbridge Regulatory CRO' placeholder/'New client?' copy to match the chosen mode.

onboarding.theme: Audit stream claimed but not viewable/exportable
onboarding.quote: give me a way to actually view that audit event stream from the account page rather than just being told it exists.
onboarding.change: Add an 'Audit log' panel on the Account & security page that renders the append-only event stream with a 'Download (CSV/JSON)' export button, so provenance can be produced, not just promised.

onboarding.quote: the 'role' needs a visible permission list... I need to know if roles enforce real segregation of duties (author/publisher/approver).
onboarding.change: On the Account page, make the 'Your role' line expand to a permission matrix listing each role (author/publisher/approver/admin) and exactly what it can do, plus who assigns it.

onboarding.quote: make MFA enforceable at the workspace level, not just opt-in per user, because 'sign-in stays password-only' if someone stops halfway is a real audit finding.
onboarding.change: Add a workspace-admin setting 'Require MFA for all members' that blocks password-only sign-in for the workspace until each user completes enrolment.

onboarding.quote: 'otpauth URI' and 'salted hashes' are gibberish to me... I don't know what half of that means and I shouldn't need to read it to log in.
onboarding.change: Move the security-plumbing terms off the login/MFA card to the Account & security page, and add a plain-language tooltip on the MFA step (e.g. 'MFA = a second code from your phone; tap this link to add it to your authenticator app').

journey.theme: Opaque 'Validation passed' / routing verdict — no rule catalogue, version, or citation
journey.quote: I'd never rely on a green 'Validation passed' checkmark unless I know it runs the current Health Canada validation criteria and eValidator-equivalent rules with a named version — regional XML, envelope, checksum, hyperlink and lifecycle-operator checks — and the walkthrough gives me a checkmark with no rule catalogue, no error detail, no spec version.
journey.change: On the Validation step, replace the '✓ Validation passed / ✗ N errors' chip with a named validation-profile + eCTD-spec-version header and an expandable, exportable error report listing each failing file, the rule ID, and a link to the Health Canada guidance the rule enforces; likewise make 'Check my pathway' show its routing rationale and cite the specific HC guidance clause behind each ANDS/NDS/SNDS verdict and warning.

journey.theme: 'Riding the US FDA gateway' framing alarms/confuses on a Canadian filing
journey.quote: seeing 'FDA' three times on a Health Canada transmission screen would make me stop and question whether this product actually understands the Canadian pathway.
journey.change: Rewrite the transmission-step copy to lead with 'Common Electronic Submissions Gateway (CESG)' instead of 'the US FDA gateway', and add an inline tooltip on each of the three receipt tiles (MDN, ACK, HC ACK/Core ID) with one plain sentence each explaining what the receipt proves and why a Canadian ANDS uses the shared gateway.

journey.theme: No compliance/record-integrity controls — audit trail, e-signature, access, data residency
journey.quote: it says 'grounded in real Health Canada process' and validates ID formats, but ... I saw nothing about an audit trail, user access controls, e-signature integrity, or where my dossier data is stored — those are the first questions I ask of any cloud tool.
journey.change: Add a visible, exportable, tamper-evident audit log (who-changed-what-when) plus a compliance panel documenting Part-11-style e-signature integrity, role-based access controls, and a data-residency statement, surfaced before the QA-review and e-signature steps rather than as one-line labels.

journey.theme: Single-submission / single-user: no portfolio, assignees, deadlines, or CDMO client segregation
journey.quote: this is all single-submission and single-user. There's no view of who's blocked on what, no assignee or due date per step, no client-facing progress export, and no portfolio roll-up across dossiers even though there's a 'Portfolio' chip up top.
journey.change: Build a portfolio dashboard behind the existing 'Portfolio' chip showing all dossiers with per-step owner, due date, and blocked/ready status, add per-client workspaces with confidentiality walls for CDMOs, and let a completed journey be cloned as a template for the next generic.

journey.theme: Company ID multi-week enrolment buried mid-journey; 'continue while pending' risks building on sand
journey.quote: the Company ID enrolment (email a template, wait ~two weeks) is buried mid-journey; that lead time should be flagged loudly on the very first screen so nobody starts a filing they can't finish.
journey.change: Add an upfront readiness-checklist screen before Step 1 listing every external prerequisite (5-digit Company ID, Dossier ID) with its expected lead time and the OSIP enrolment template link, and turn 'I've requested it — continue while it's pending' into a tracked open-risk item with a reminder that flags any dossier built on an unconfirmed Company ID.

journey.theme: Document assembly / eCTD Module builder split onto a separate page breaks the guided flow
journey.quote: don't hide the Module builder behind an 'Open the Module builder →' link on a separate dossiers page — bouncing between the wizard and a separate assembly surface is exactly the context-switching that costs me time in eCTD Office today.
journey.change: Embed the eCTD Module 1-5 builder inline as the document-placement step of the journey (keeping the readiness gate that disables Continue until required documents are placed) instead of linking out to a separate dossiers page.

journey.theme: Lifecycle blindness: no sequence numbers, submission types, or new/replace/append/delete operators
journey.quote: the walkthrough never once mentions how it handles a lifecycle sequence versus an initial filing — and an ANDS is almost never a single one-and-done submission.
journey.change: Add explicit sequence numbering and a submission-type/lifecycle-operator selector (new/replace/append/delete) to the journey, with support for supplements (SNDS) and clarifax/deficiency responses, rather than modelling only a one-and-done initial filing.

journey.theme: No bilingual / Module 1 labelling support (French PM, mock-ups, XML PM)
journey.quote: add explicit bilingual/Module 1 support — French product monograph and mock-up handling — because without it I can't call this 'guided end to end' for a Canadian ANDS.
journey.change: Surface Module 1 labelling requirements explicitly in the document-placement step — checklist items for bilingual (English/French) product monographs and mock-ups plus the XML Product Monograph format — and have validation flag missing French content.

catalog.theme: Native browser prompt/confirm for rename & delete
catalog.quote: deleting a dossier "and all of its documents" is gated only by a native browser confirm dialog with a warning that it "cannot be undone" - in a validated environment I need an audit trail, role-based permission, and ideally a recoverable soft-delete, not a one-click irreversible wipe
catalog.change: Replace the window.prompt/window.confirm on the tile's rename and delete (✕) actions with in-app modals: the delete modal requires typing the exact Dossier ID to enable the Delete button and performs a recoverable soft-delete (Trash/Archive with undo) instead of a hard, irreversible delete.

catalog.theme: No audit trail / Part-11 controls on destructive actions
catalog.quote: There's no mention of version history, who-did-what logging, or Part-11-style controls on any of these actions, and that's exactly what I'd be asked about in an inspection
catalog.change: On dossier rename, delete, and placeholder-to-real-ID change, write a timestamped audit-log entry (user, action, before/after ID, reason-for-change field) surfaced in a per-dossier History panel.

catalog.quote: "CS-BE" and the "submission type" meta line are stated but never explained, and I'd want to know where that classification comes from
catalog.change: Make CS-BE an explicit, user-selected submission-type field at dossier creation (not a hardcoded chip), and add hover tooltips on the tile expanding CS-BE, eCTD Module 1–5, REP, and CESG.

catalog.theme: Placeholder "d" ID could leak into a real filing
catalog.quote: I'd want to see that a placeholder "d"-prefixed ID can't leak into an actual eCTD envelope or filename, because a fake ID escaping into a sequence would be a hard reject at the CESG gateway
catalog.change: Show a persistent colored "draft ID — set real" warning badge on any placeholder-ID tile and hard-block export/filing (not just a soft reminder) until a valid one-letter+6–7-digit real Dossier ID replaces the placeholder.

catalog.quote: A "Ready to file" chip worries me if it's derived from module count rather than a real eValidator-grade pass
catalog.change: Add a tooltip on the "Ready to file" / "3/5 modules" chip stating exactly what it checks (e.g. Module 1–5 content presence vs. eValidator-grade validation pass) so it isn't mistaken for filing clearance.

catalog.quote: a grid of tiles doesn't answer the status-call questions I actually get asked
catalog.change: Add search/filter plus per-tile owner/assignee, due-date, and client/sponsor grouping fields to the catalog so PMs and multi-sponsor CDMOs can triage dozens of dossiers.

catalog.theme: No bilingual (FR/EN) indication despite bilingual Module 1
catalog.quote: this walkthrough is entirely in English with no sign of French anywhere, and Module 1 labelling in Canada is bilingual by law
catalog.change: Add a bilingual (FR/EN) status indicator on each dossier tile reflecting Module 1's required French/English content state.

builder_forms.theme: Sample pre-fill can slip into a live filing
builder_forms.quote: Pre-populating regulatory fields with "realistic samples" from another dossier is a data-integrity landmine; one associate under deadline who skims instead of replacing a "sample" field and you've cross-contaminated a client's s.5 statement or reference product.
builder_forms.change: Make sample-tagged fields hard-blocking: a section cannot be marked complete and the "Author"/"Ready to file" action stays disabled until every sample-tagged field has been affirmatively edited (touched + confirmed), captured in the audit log, with a final "N sample values remain" pre-file gate; default sample data OFF (empty fields with the example shown as non-savable ghost/placeholder text).

builder_forms.theme: "Health Canada review / Valid eCTD" overpromises vs real validation
builder_forms.quote: "no blocking content gaps" is a content-completeness check, not eCTD validation — I see nothing about XML backbone correctness, leaf/lifecycle operators, checksums matching the backbone, or an eValidator-equivalent pass.
builder_forms.change: Rename "Health Canada review" to "Draft completeness check" and replace the single "Valid eCTD" flag with an itemized report naming the validator, spec/DTD/validation-profile version and date, and pass/fail per rule, explicitly stating it checks presence/format not scientific adequacy or eCTD technical validation.

builder_forms.theme: Regulatory field labels lack plain-language help
builder_forms.quote: terms like "s.5 statement (per patent)", "AUC 90% CI", and "Canadian Reference Product" are thrown at me with labels only and no plain-English explanation, so I'd still be Googling half of them or calling my consultant.
builder_forms.change: Add a hover tooltip / inline glossary popover on every regulatory field label (s.5 statement, AUC 90% CI, Canadian Reference Product) giving a one-line plain-English definition, so non-expert users (founders, juniors, newcomers) don't tab out to look them up.

builder_forms.quote: What's unclear is what "Author in-app" actually produces: it says the document "lists above the tabs with filename, size, md5 fragment" but never tells me the output format — is it a compliant PDF/A, is it going into a leaf with correct eCTD placement, or just a rendered form?
builder_forms.change: On the Author panel, state the output artifact explicitly (e.g. "produces a PDF/A leaf placed at eCTD 1.2.5 with lifecycle operator = new") and surface the leaf format, placement, and lifecycle operator per authored document.

builder_forms.quote: a circle versus a half-circle means nothing to me without a legend... put plain words next to those glyphs; a legend buried somewhere isn't good enough for a document this consequential.
builder_forms.change: Add a persistent, always-visible legend (or text labels beside each glyph) in the section tree mapping the empty/half/check/N-A circles to "Not started / In progress / Complete / N-A", rather than relying on a buried or hover-only key.

builder_forms.theme: No French/bilingual PM XML handling or multi-client dossier isolation
builder_forms.quote: I see nothing here about French translations or PM XML conformance — a form that pre-fills English sample text is honestly a liability in my world.
builder_forms.change: Add explicit bilingual French/English handling and a Product Monograph XML validity check to the Module 1 readiness rail, plus a per-dossier data-isolation attestation ensuring one sponsor's dossier never seeds another's sample data.

ai_draft.theme: Review-vs-HC step is optional and off-screen
ai_draft.quote: a chip and a hidden live-region message are not controls — the actual verification against guidance is optional and easy to skip, and I'm accountable for that content, not the model.
ai_draft.change: After 'Use this draft', render an on-screen blocking 'Review vs Health Canada' step on the saved-document card that must be run before the section can count as complete / before the 'Valid eCTD' gate flag turns green.

ai_draft.theme: Post-save review instruction only in screen-reader live region
ai_draft.quote: the instruction to go run the review step is only announced to a screen reader, so a sighted user just sees the document appear with no on-screen prompt that a required-elements check still has to happen.
ai_draft.change: Move the 'AI-assisted draft saved — now run Review vs Health Canada before filing' message out of the aria-live-only region into a persistent visible banner on the saved-document card for all users.

ai_draft.theme: 'Author' button pointer points to wrong mode
ai_draft.quote: the not-configured message points to an 'Author' button that doesn't exist where it says; a first-timer under deadline pressure will hunt for it and give up.
ai_draft.change: Fix the no-GROQ_API_KEY fallback copy and the save-confirmation copy so the 'Author' button reference names its real location (under 'Sample & edit'), or relocate the button to be literally below the chat where the text says.

ai_draft.theme: Overlapping mode/tab sprawl (Draft with AI vs Sample & edit)
ai_draft.quote: 'Author,' 'Draft with AI,' and 'Sample & edit' are three overlapping doors... the crucial 'Review vs Health Canada' check is buried under the OTHER mode.
ai_draft.change: Collapse the 'Draft with AI' / 'Sample & edit' sibling toggle into one authoring panel so the Review action and Author fallback live in the same mode where the user drafted, instead of behind a separate toggle.

ai_draft.theme: md5/checksum is not real eCTD validation
ai_draft.quote: a checksum tells me nothing about eCTD validity, correct XML backbone placement, leaf/lifecycle operators, or whether the content actually satisfies the M2/M3 requirement.
ai_draft.change: Tie the 'Valid eCTD' gate to an actual eValidator-style pass showing required-element coverage and backbone/leaf placement, and surface inline which required elements are still missing — not just an md5 prefix.

ai_draft.theme: No data-residency / third-party LLM confidentiality statement
ai_draft.quote: leaning on GROQ_API_KEY tells me my sponsors' dossier content is going to a third-party LLM... until I see the data-handling and per-client isolation terms in writing, that alone would stop me deploying this.
ai_draft.change: Add a data-residency and per-client confidentiality line directly on the AI badge tooltip stating where GROQ-processed dossier text is sent and how per-sponsor isolation is enforced.

ai_draft.theme: No bilingual French / XML Product Monograph support
ai_draft.quote: nothing here speaks to my reality: no mention of bilingual French drafting or XML Product Monograph structure, which is half my job.
ai_draft.change: Add a French-language draft/reconcile companion and an XML Product Monograph template mode to the authoring panel for labelling sections, alongside the English draft.

validate_export.quote: if the validator is offline, the export proceeds silently without a check — silently exporting an unvalidated package is exactly how a screening rejection happens
validate_export.change: Make the export path fail closed: when the validator is unreachable, hard-block the Export button and show a red 'Validation could not run — export blocked' state; if any override is allowed at all, force an explicit 'validation skipped' acknowledgement watermarked on the output and written to the Audit trail, never a quiet download.

validate_export.theme: CA-E/CA-W codes are 'validation-rule-style', not the real HC criteria
validate_export.quote: 'validation-rule-style IDs' is not the same as being validated against the current Health Canada eCTD Validation Criteria... a home-grown look-alike ruleset with unknown coverage cannot replace that
validate_export.change: On the eCTD validation card, replace the 'validation-rule-style' footnote with a stated Health Canada eCTD Validation Criteria version/date and map each CA-E/CA-W finding to its published HC/eValidator rule number, plus a coverage statement listing which rule families are and are not checked.

validate_export.theme: Flimsy browser confirm() as the export/override gate
validate_export.quote: a plain browser confirm dialog to override 3 unresolved errors and 'Export anyway' is exactly the kind of one-click bypass that fails an audit
validate_export.change: Replace the native confirm() on export-with-errors with an in-app modal that lists the specific unresolved CA-E findings and requires a typed reason, capturing the overrider's identity, timestamp and validator version to the Audit trail (Part-11-style).

validate_export.theme: Rule codes lack plain-language meaning and fix guidance
validate_export.quote: a rule code like 'CA-E' tells me nothing about what I actually did wrong or how to fix it, and the footnote just piles on more jargon
validate_export.change: Make each CA-E/CA-W finding in the error list clickable to a plain-English panel stating what the rule means, which document/leaf is at fault, and how to fix it, with a citation to the underlying Health Canada rule.

validate_export.theme: Structural PASS vs separate 'Run full check (PDF conformance)' ambiguity
validate_export.quote: if the badge says PASSED but the deep PDF check hasn't run, I don't know from this description whether I'm actually cleared
validate_export.change: Run the PDF-conformance check automatically as part of Export (or make the 'Valid eCTD' flag only turn green after it passes) and, until it has run, show the readiness flag in a distinct 'structural only — PDF conformance not yet run' state that blocks a clean PASSED badge.

validate_export.theme: Dense side-rail layout and confusing sequence state (working/ACTIVE/Make active)
validate_export.quote: 'working: 0001' versus 'ACTIVE' sequence distinction is the kind of thing that trips people up under deadline pressure
validate_export.change: Add an inline helper/tooltip on the Sequences card defining working vs ACTIVE and what 'Make active' does, and a short 'what is a sequence / when to create one' primer surfaced next to those controls for first-time users.

validate_export.theme: No PM rollup / no bilingual-French Module 1 completeness check
validate_export.quote: give me a PM-facing rollup - deadline, who's blocked, error count in plain terms - so I don't have to decode CA-E codes
validate_export.change: Add a per-dossier plain-English status roll-up (deadline, blocked section/owner, error count in plain terms) for PMs, and add a readiness rule that flags a missing or mismatched French Module 1 document/mock-up before export.

operations.quote: a bare countdown I can't audit is worse than none... let me click 'NOA: 12d' and see the served date and the rule it's counting from
operations.change: On every day-counter chip (45-day window, 24-month stay, NOA, OVERDUE Right-to-Sell), make the number click-to-expand a provenance popover showing the anchor date, its source (ingested notice vs hand-keyed), calendar-vs-business-day basis, the counting rule with an HC/PMNOC citation, and a 'computed — verify independently' disclaimer.

operations.theme: Acronym overload with no inline glossary
operations.quote: the Correspondence page is a wall of acronyms... put plain-English tooltips or a one-line 'what is this / when does it apply' on every acronym (SAL, NOA, Form V, s.6)
operations.change: Add hover tooltips on every regulatory acronym (SAL/SDN/SRL/NOC/NOD/NON/NOA/Form V/s.6/24-month stay) at each point of use on the Correspondence and Registry pages, each giving a one-line plain-English definition plus 'when this applies'.

operations.quote: make the 'this is a record, not a submission to Health Canada' boundary loud and repeated on every action button, not buried in a Help link
operations.change: Add a persistent 'Record only — does not transmit to Health Canada' banner on the Correspondence page and an inline confirmation on action buttons like 'Ingest SAL' and 'Serve NOA' stating the action only logs a record and does not file with HC.

operations.quote: I'd want a confirmation or 'are you sure' step on the status transition buttons like '→ Marketed', since those look one-click and irreversible-scary
operations.change: Add an 'are you sure?' confirmation dialog (stating reversibility) to irreversible dossier status transitions such as '→ Marketed', and require an effective date plus reason captured to the audit stream on confirm.

operations.quote: My hard blocker before adopting is multi-client data isolation — nothing here tells me one sponsor's dossiers, DINs or NOA clocks can't leak into another's workspace
operations.change: Add an explicit per-client workspace scope with a visible client column on the Portfolio grid and access-scoping controls, so a CDMO can see and enforce that one sponsor's dossiers/DINs/NOA clocks are segregated from another's.

operations.theme: No owner/assignee per dossier for status reporting
operations.quote: I can see a dossier is '3/7 modules' and blocked, but not who owns it or who I need to chase, which is the first question on every status call
operations.change: Add an owner/assignee field to each dossier row on the Portfolio grid (included in the CSV export) plus a portfolio-wide deadline rollup, so a PM can see who is blocked on what.

operations.quote: the complete absence of anything bilingual or labelling-facing — I would add a clear French-language indication and some sign of Module 1 product-monograph handling
operations.change: Add a visible bilingual (EN/FR) language indicator and a note on the Portfolio page stating where Module 1 product-monograph/labelling work lives (or that it is out of scope), so labelling specialists know whether the tool serves them.

overall.theme: No proof of eCTD technical validation / Health Canada-acceptable output
overall.quote: a submission I can trust must produce a valid eCTD/regional backbone that passes Health Canada's validator, and this walkthrough never claims that.
overall.change: Add a 'Validation' panel to the readiness card that runs a named, versioned Health Canada eCTD validation profile and renders a downloadable validator report (rule pass/fail, ToC/hyperlink integrity, index-md5) before the 'Ready to file' chip can turn green.

overall.theme: 'Readiness %' is undefined — unclear what it measures against
overall.quote: '34% ready' means nothing to me without knowing it maps to real conformance
overall.change: Make the readiness % chip expand into an itemized breakdown that states its denominator (e.g. 'X of Y Health Canada screening/validation rules passed') and links each missing item to the named HC requirement behind it.

overall.quote: the absence of SSO is a hard blocker for onboarding a team of nine under our IT policy
overall.change: Publish a dated SAML/OIDC SSO item on a visible product Roadmap card on the Account & security page, with target release quarter.

overall.theme: Acronyms/regulatory gates unexplained inline; novice hits ID gate cold
overall.quote: explain the acronyms inline where they appear (a hover or 'what's this?' on REP/CESG/TOTP)
overall.change: Surface the Dossier ID format rule and placeholder option BEFORE the field errors, and add inline hover/'what's this?' explainers on first use of REP, CESG, TOTP, ANDS, and M1-M5 (with a 'you'll need these before you file' checklist).

overall.theme: '3D submission tower' reads as gimmick, undermines regulatory seriousness
overall.quote: the 3D submission tower does nothing for me; I'd rather that panel show a plain checklist of outstanding items I can hand to a reviewer.
overall.change: Replace (or make optional/toggle to) the 3D submission tower with a plain printable checklist mapping each module tile to the specific Health Canada requirement it satisfies and its outstanding items.

overall.theme: No portfolio/PM layer — owners, due dates, blockers, exportable status
overall.quote: add a team and timeline layer - assign owners to modules, show due dates and blockers, and give me an exportable portfolio-level status report, because right now 'Portfolio' is just a chip with no described function.
overall.change: Build out the 'Portfolio' chip into a real dashboard listing each dossier's readiness %, target file date, owner, and blocker, with a one-click exportable weekly client status report.

overall.theme: No mention of bilingual French labelling / XML Product Monograph
overall.quote: the entire overall concept is silent on bilingual/French content and the XML PM tooling that Health Canada mandates for monographs
overall.change: Add explicit bilingual French/English handling and XML Product Monograph export to the Module 1 workspace, and state on the overview that M1 manages the paired French/English dossier and exports the mandated XML PM structure.
